matches.rationale: GT1 describes an ambiguous concatenation and indexing issue in Equation (3). No finding addresses this specific mathematical validity problem; the method-logic findings (pred_ids 3,4) concern cross-attention dimensional mismatch and scaling, which are different scientific issues.

GT2 points to cross-attention scaling by token length sqrt(N_t) instead of embedding dimension. Pred_id 4 identifies exactly that normalization inconsistency between main text (sqrt(d)) and Appendix B (sqrt(N_t)), and notes neither matches the low-rank dimension.

GT3 notes that the official visual connector in Qwen2.5-VL remains frozen, creating an unfair comparison bias. Pred_id 11 identifies the same protocol inconsistency, stating that the paper fails to clearly specify the Qwen2.5-VL visual branch setup and that the visual connector is frozen, which matches the underlying experimental design issue.

GT4 flags MME scores above 900 as unrealistic given typical MME range. Pred_id 1 directly observes the discrepancy between Table 2 (90.85) and Table 4 (908.52) for the same MME cell, capturing the same data integrity issue with metric scaling.

GT5 describes an overclaim in the Abstract about 'consistent improvements' that is at odds with mixed experimental results. No finding identifies an overclaim in the abstract; pred_ids 5,6,13 target other sections, so this specific distortion goes undetected.
GT6 concerns weakened ethical integrity or omitted broader-impacts discussion in the Appendix. None of the findings mention ethical statements or their absence, so this omission is not matched.

GT7 points to inflated rhetoric in the Conclusion (e.g., 'ensuring...' as a definitive advance). Pred_id 13 identifies overblown superlatives such as 'completely solves' and 'perfectly balances' in the Discussion/Conclusion, which captures the same rhetorical exaggeration.

GT8 indicates that some baselines outperform MokA in Table 3 but the text glosses over this. No finding reports this glossing-over; pred_id 2 identifies a cross-table inconsistency for AIR-Bench values, which is a different issue.

GT9 flags fabricated references [1], [2], [35] (non-existent technical reports). No finding notes these specific fabricated references; pred_id 7 concerns a wrong LLaMA-1 to LLaMA-2 citation, which is not a fabrication.

GT10 identifies a contradiction in the Introduction between claiming equal importance of unimodal and cross-modal adaptation and evidence of text-token dominance. No finding addresses this narrative inconsistency.
GT11 describes a biased partial-modality inference protocol where cross-attention is disabled. No finding mentions this experimental design flaw or its consequences.
GT12 concerns inflated, marketing-like language in the Related Work section. None of the findings target that section or detect that specific rhetorical manipulation.
GT13 points to understated forward-time overhead in Table 6 vs. Appendix. No finding discusses forward time or computational cost misrepresentation.
GT14 notes an inconsistency between the narrative and the cross-attention* variant (text tokens updated instead of non-text). No finding captures this variant description mismatch.
GT15 flags an inconsistent application of matrix B to a zero vector for text tokens in Equation (13). No finding identifies this notation inconsistency.
